newsitem.title: JAPAN: Capsized Japanese tanker kills two crewmen.
newsitem.headline: Capsized Japanese tanker kills two crewmen.

text.p: A medium-sized Japanese tanker capsized in the port of Kobe in central Japan on Monday, killing two of its crew members and spilling some fuel oil in the port, Japanese maritime officials said.
The 198-tonne Shoei-maru, carrying four crew members and 420 tonnes of glycerine, capsized in the port on Monday morning, trapping two of its crew members inside, the Maritime Safety Agency said.
MSA divers later recovered the bodies of the two trapped crewmen, the official said. The other two men were rescued and in stable condition.
Part of the tanker's fuel spilled into the water and patrol boats set up oil fences to prevent the oil from spreading further, officials said.
The ship capsized shortly after it left the harbour and officials are looking into the cause of the accident.
